questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the destination, due to the fact that it was my fathers birthplace and because I was interested in Learning the Egyptian dialect first and foremost.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience and would definetely recommend it to others looking to learn arabic. Alexandria is a great place to be in regard to egyptian culture and language.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Didn't face any problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They assisted me with a guided tour around the city, so that I would be more familiar with the city and together with the other students, which was great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found acommodation on AirBnb, it worked very well and I spoke to the landlord before arrival which was very calming. Although Airbnb may be a bit more expensive than other options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will take time to get used to the cities rhythm and the lifestyle, but by living away from campus you are forced into daily egyptian life which is great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general the host institution had a few options although not great, but the availability in the city itself is great and reasonably priced.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Did not encounter any problems, filled out a form and sent them a copy of my passport prior to arriving, luckily I'm off egyptian origin, so a visa wasn't neccesary for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very helpfull with regards to any problems or diffuculties there might be present.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Had no issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the guidelines and respond to the mails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have any diffuculties although, it was a bit dissapointing that there were no exact classes suited to my particular level until the last month.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were a substitute for 30 ECTS points in total, and the level was therefor high regarding obligatory presence but also homework everyday.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's obviously different and I feel you need to get used to it being in arabic only. I faced diffuculties with the level in the beginning especially and in the difference in classes. It's centered about glossary and different texts a lot and the computer is rarely needed or advised for that matter.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECA (Egyptian Colloquial Arabic) 
MSA (Modern Standard Arabic)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECA is very neccesary for communicating in Egypt as the dialect is very different from MSA.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately I faced an injury in my lower back in the beginning of my stay so had some medical bills.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheap and you can eat really cheap if you want to. Domestic flights are more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offer 4 different clubs including, singing, caligraphy, movie and cooking club, which is nice. And they were good at hosting social events during the stay such as iftar dinner and social meetings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the cooking club and the caligraphy if you are interested in art and such.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The library in Alexandria. Montazah Garden, Castle of Qaitbay, roman Amfitheater at Kum El Dikkah and obviously just walking in the center of Mahattet Raml, Manshiyah and Nabi Daniel.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It takes some time to get used to the difference in culture and traffic, language barrier and so on. But eventually it will grow on you and you will start to feel at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's extreamly easy in Egypt because Egyptians are very curious people and very welcoming, an easy place to make new friends for sure.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Think the fact that the culture is centered around late night activity and I prefer to go to bed a bit earlier and it will still be noisy after 0000, but it is quiet in the morning. If you look different people will stare and that might be diffucult for a lot of people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like that most people are very welcoming and warm towards you

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's hardest in the beginning, but will get easier. 

Expect a difference in the way the university is run and try not to compare it too much to your own university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy food at local markets if you want cheap but fresh fruit and vege. Try out Talabat, it works extreamly well in Egypt if you are lazy with dinner or shopping.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definetely to get an insight to having an everyday life in a different country and trying to learn the language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes you feel homesick and are in desperate need of peace and quiet.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
